$comment: What a DEPLOYED cezar means, as probes a machine can run. The `deploy` step of the
spec-to-deploy workflow is green only when EVERY target below exits 0 — see
.ai/specs/2026-08-20-steps-green-only-when-verified.md and workflows/postconditions.ts.
cezar is TWO services and shipping one alone used to end that step green.
Each probe runs with bash -lc in the step's cwd, bounded at 60s.
DELIVERY IS NOT ACTIVATION: the service probe deliberately checks that the running
process answers, not merely that a new dist tree was copied into place — a half-live
deploy (new CLI tree, old resident server) is exactly what reads like a whole one.
CORRECTED 2026-08-21: the backend probe used to compare `/opt/cezar/.deployed-commit`
against HEAD. On a rootless blue-green box that file is never written (`/opt/cezar` is a
symlink into /opt/cezar-releases/, and `deploy.json` + GET /api/v1/health's `deploy`
field are the ledger), so the probe failed after a WORKING deploy — a red that says
nothing about the deploy. It now asks the RUNNING process which sha it is serving,
which is strictly stronger: a stale marker cannot forge it. `.deployed-commit` stays as
a fallback for boxes still on the --strategy=restart path, which do write it.

CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-08-21 (later the same day). The correction above fixed WHAT the backend probe asks but left HOW it asks broken, and it read red twice more after deploys that had worked. Two defects, both fixed here.

(1) SILENT RED. It took ONE 10s shot at GET /api/v1/health under `set -e`, so a slow answer killed the probe at `test -n $live` — BEFORE the diagnostic echo — and the step reported "(no output)", indistinguishable from a real failure. /health is the wrong endpoint for a deploy gate: it is cached stale-while-revalidate and past HEALTH_MAX_STALE_MS (60s) the read BLOCKS on a fresh snapshot, which server.ts:2076 documents as ~0.8s of agent-CLI --version spawns plus ~0.4s of git — easily over 10s on a loaded box. That is what failed at 20:48:16Z while the UI probe, hitting the same server, passed. It now polls GET /api/v1/ready — uncached by construction, 503 until actually ready, carrying the same deploy field — and WAITS on that condition in a 30s bounded loop (the harness SIGKILLs a probe at PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS=60s, so the budget stays well inside it). The 2s poll interval is the doctrine's sanctioned until-loop, not a guessed sleep N.

(2) EXACT EQUALITY ON A SHARED BOX. It demanded live sha == this worktree HEAD. cezar is ONE service and concurrent tasks deploy their own HEADs, so a task whose HEAD was not the exact live sha read red even though its code was running — which happened at 20:50:44Z when a concurrent task activated 7e8f2938 over this run's 2438b6d7. HEAD being an ANCESTOR of the live sha is now green, and that is not a weakening: everything at HEAD is in the running process. A server BEHIND this HEAD, or on a divergent line, is still red.

The SAME rewrite was applied to the UI probe (2026-08-21, run e06f2169). It is listed under the correction above rather than as a new one because it had BOTH of those defects and neither was fixed when the backend probe was: it took one 10s shot under `set -e` and could only ever fail as "(no output)", and it raced the cutover it verifies. It stayed green through the incident by luck — it hits `/`, a static route that never takes the cached-/health path that actually timed out — so nothing had forced the issue. Fixing one of two targets and leaving the other is the exact shape this file exists to prevent: cezar is TWO services, and a half-verified deploy reads like a whole one. It cannot use /api/v1/ready, because the thing it must prove is that the HTML actually served names this build's bundle, so it polls `/` on the same 30s/2s bounded loop and names its reason.

CORRECTED 2026-08-24: both targets became "manual": true here (owner decision, commit c328ec06, .ai/specs/2026-08-24-default-workflow-ten-stages.md D6). A person activates cezar now, not an agent: see each target's manualReason for the exact command. BOTH targets are manual, not the backend alone, because prod-host's blue-green activation is ONE atomic symlink flip that restarts the whole service; marking only the backend manual would let an agent "legitimately" activate the UI target and flip the same symlink anyway, which is the half-truth this entry exists to close. A red here, with a manual-deploy handoff attached, is a PARK awaiting a human, not a failed deploy: see .ai/specs/2026-08-24-manual-deploy-not-a-bug.md.

CORRECTED 2026-08-26: the manualReason above used to say deploy THIS RUN’S OWN WORKTREE. It now says activate origin/main, with the worktree kept as the named exception for a run that never landed. Measured that day: live was dc64b741 (2026-08-25T10:34Z) while origin/main was d20f7101 (2026-08-26T11:08Z) — 18 commits and ~25h behind — and every run that finished in that window sat on its own copy of this card, all of them waiting on the SAME single action. Stage 8 lands a run on the base branch before this step runs, so main already contains the HEAD and one activation satisfies every parked run whose HEAD is an ancestor of it. The backend probe’s ancestor test was fixed in the same change and for the same reason: `--is-ancestor` exits non-zero for BOTH "not an ancestor" and "unknown object", so the old `2>/dev/null` would have reported a CORRECT activation of main as a red the moment the worktree had not fetched it. A restart now re-probes every manual-deploy park (recover()), because on this box an activation IS a restart — so the operator presses Resolve zero times, not once per parked run. See .ai/specs/2026-08-26-activate-main-not-worktrees.md.

targets.name: cezar service (backend) — the RUNNING process is ready and serving this HEAD
targets.manualReason: a person activates cezar, not an agent (owner decision 2026-08-24, .ai/specs/2026-08-24-default-workflow-ten-stages.md D6 — unchanged). CORRECTED 2026-08-26: activate origin/main, NOT this run's own worktree. Stage 8 lands the run on the base branch before this step runs, so origin/main already contains this HEAD, and ONE activation clears EVERY parked run at once instead of one card per run. On prod-host, as cezar (never root): bash scripts/activate-main.sh. By hand that is: cd /var/lib/cezar/deploy/cezar && git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/main && npm ci && npm run build && node /opt/cezar/packages/cezar/dist/index.js server-deploy --strategy=blue-green --source="$PWD" --sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD)". NOT the shared checkout /var/lib/cezar/loki-labs/cezar (task worktrees fork from it), and NOT an unmerged worktree (it ships a tree the merged-tree gate never saw, and it cannot clear a sibling run on a divergent line). THE EXCEPTION: if this HEAD is not on the base branch then landing was skipped, and only then deploy this run’s own worktree, the path the run reports — keeping --source pointed at it, because server-deploy builds whatever is checked out while --sha only labels the release (KB notion-8d2aa351272c). Activation is one atomic symlink flip that restarts the service, so do it when the board is quiet. Verify with curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:4321/api/v1/ready and check deploy.sha. You should NOT need to press Resolve: the restart re-probes every parked manual-deploy run and continues the ones now covered (.ai/specs/2026-08-26-activate-main-not-worktrees.md S4).
targets.probe:
set -u
# Deliberately NOT `set -e`: the old probe died silently mid-pipeline and reported "(no output)",
# which is indistinguishable from a real red. Every exit below names its reason.
test -f /opt/cezar/packages/cezar/dist/index.js || { echo "no deployed tree: /opt/cezar/packages/cezar/dist/index.js is missing"; exit 1; }
head=$(git rev-parse HEAD) || { echo "git rev-parse HEAD failed in $PWD"; exit 1; }
live=''
deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + 30 ))
while :; do
  live=$(curl -fsS --max-time 10 http://127.0.0.1:4321/api/v1/ready 2>/dev/null | grep -o '"deploy":{[^}]*}' | grep -o '"sha":"[0-9a-f]*"' | grep -o '[0-9a-f]\{7,40\}' | head -1)
  [ -n "$live" ] && break
  [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "$deadline" ] && break
  sleep 2
done
[ -n "$live" ] || live=$(grep -oE '^[0-9a-f]{7,40}' /opt/cezar/.deployed-commit 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$live" ] || { echo "no deploy sha after 30s: GET /api/v1/ready never returned one (unreachable, 503 draining/not-ready, or too old to carry a deploy field) and /opt/cezar/.deployed-commit is absent"; exit 1; }
case "$head" in "$live"*) echo "live=$live == HEAD"; exit 0;; esac
# The ancestor test needs $live IN THIS WORKTREE’S OBJECT DB. `--is-ancestor` exits non-zero for BOTH
# "not an ancestor" and "unknown object", and the old `2>/dev/null` printed the first reading for both.
# Deploying origin/main ARMS that: a worktree cut before those commits existed has never fetched the sha,
# so a CORRECT activation would have read as "NOT serving this HEAD". Resolve it first, then ask.
git cat-file -e "$live^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || git fetch --quiet origin 2>/dev/null
git cat-file -e "$live^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || { echo "live=$live head=$head — the live sha is not in this worktree’s object db even after a fetch, so its relation to HEAD CANNOT BE DETERMINED (which is not the same as \"not deployed\")"; exit 1; }
# No `2>/dev/null` here: the object is now proven present, so any remaining error is real.
git merge-base --is-ancestor "$head" "$live" && { echo "live=$live contains HEAD=$head — this HEAD is running (the activation deployed origin/main, or a concurrent task deployed a later commit)"; exit 0; }
echo "live=$live head=$head — the running server is NOT serving this HEAD"
exit 1

targets.name: cezar UI (web) — the built bundle is the one being served
targets.manualReason: a person activates cezar, not an agent (owner decision 2026-08-24, .ai/specs/2026-08-24-default-workflow-ten-stages.md D6 — unchanged). CORRECTED 2026-08-26: activate origin/main, NOT this run's own worktree. Stage 8 lands the run on the base branch before this step runs, so origin/main already contains this HEAD, and ONE activation clears EVERY parked run at once instead of one card per run. On prod-host, as cezar (never root): bash scripts/activate-main.sh. By hand that is: cd /var/lib/cezar/deploy/cezar && git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/main && npm ci && npm run build && node /opt/cezar/packages/cezar/dist/index.js server-deploy --strategy=blue-green --source="$PWD" --sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD)". NOT the shared checkout /var/lib/cezar/loki-labs/cezar (task worktrees fork from it), and NOT an unmerged worktree (it ships a tree the merged-tree gate never saw, and it cannot clear a sibling run on a divergent line). THE EXCEPTION: if this HEAD is not on the base branch then landing was skipped, and only then deploy this run’s own worktree, the path the run reports — keeping --source pointed at it, because server-deploy builds whatever is checked out while --sha only labels the release (KB notion-8d2aa351272c). Activation is one atomic symlink flip that restarts the service, so do it when the board is quiet. Verify with curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:4321/api/v1/ready and check deploy.sha. You should NOT need to press Resolve: the restart re-probes every parked manual-deploy run and continues the ones now covered (.ai/specs/2026-08-26-activate-main-not-worktrees.md S4).
targets.probe:
set -u
# Deliberately NOT `set -e`, and bounded-polling rather than one-shot, for the SAME two reasons
# the backend probe above was rewritten — this target had both defects and kept them.
idx=/opt/cezar/packages/cezar/web/dist/index.html
test -f "$idx" || { echo "no built UI: $idx is missing"; exit 1; }
asset=$(grep -o 'assets/index-[A-Za-z0-9_-]*\.js' "$idx" | head -1)
[ -n "$asset" ] || { echo "$idx names no assets/index-*.js bundle — that tree is not a vite build"; exit 1; }
why="GET / never answered in 30s — the server is unreachable or still starting"
deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + 30 ))
while :; do
  body=$(curl -fsS --max-time 10 http://127.0.0.1:4321/ 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -n "$body" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$body" | grep -qF "$asset" && { echo "serving $asset == the built bundle"; exit 0; }
    why="GET / answered but references no $asset — the served HTML is not this build"
  fi
  [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "$deadline" ] && break
  sleep 2
done
echo "$why"
exit 1
